name: Rope hammer curl
cue: Pin your elbows to your sides and curl, palms facing in.
research: Cable rope hammer curl at a low pulley, standing facing the column (feet hip-width, knees soft), elbows pinned at the sides, neutral grip (palms facing each other) on the two rope ends. ExRx (cable hammer curl): target brachioradialis, synergists brachialis and biceps brachii; keep the elbows at the sides and curl until the forearms are vertical-ish, then lower. Jeff Nippard ranks hammer curls A tier: the neutral grip takes the biceps out of supination (it is a supinator as well as an elbow flexor), so less biceps and a very active brachialis, the big flexor under the biceps; the brachioradialis flexes the elbow in every forearm position (Boland, Spigelman and Uhl 2008, J Hand Surg 33:1853-9), and the neutral grip is its strongest line of pull. Drawn: shoulder flexion 8 -> 15.1 (the elbows drift ~7 deg forward at the top, as they do with a still upper arm), abduction 5.6 (forearms in sagittal planes, fists in front of the thighs at the bottom: elbow 15 rather than 0 so they clear the thighs), elbow 15 -> 125. Each rope end rides on a hidden hinge through the circumcentre of the FK grip at the start, mid and end (via key M carries the exact mid angle; tools/design/hammer_curl.mjs), so the IK only corrects millimetres and the fist turns with the rope end; the knob is on the thumb side, the strand leaves the little-finger side and both strands (0.16 H) meet at the knot, which hangs on the cable line to the low pulley. The column stands 0.44 H (78 cm) in front of the stance, the pulley in a fork on its base; the cable leaves the knot 48 deg below horizontal at the stretch (the hanging forearm still has a moment arm against it) and the stack rises 1:1 with the cable (34 cm). Primary: brachialis and brachioradialis (labels Brachialis, Forearms); secondary: biceps.

camera.note: Research view: the right profile (az 90, el 5), square to the sagittal plane the forearms curl in. Turned 27 deg toward the front and raised 7 deg (az 63, el 12: 27.9 deg in all): the near arm shows the brachialis as a band on the outer lower upper arm, between the amber biceps in front and the triceps behind, and the brachioradialis along the thumb side of the forearm; at the peak they make one ember V around the elbow. From the true profile the two read as thin edge-on stripes (phone stage glow about 370 CSS px at the stretch and the peak, against about 730 / 550 here). Fill 0.64: the arms are a small part of a standing figure. fitMachine false: the column may crop at the top; the cable still shows where the load comes from.
